newsitem.title: USA: General Growth buys remaining stake in mall.
newsitem.headline: General Growth buys remaining stake in mall.

text.p: General Growth Properties Inc said Thursday it acquired the 61.8 percent stake in Eden Prairie Center, an Eden Prairie, Minn. mall that it did not already indirectly own.

General Growth purchased the mall from GGP/Homart Inc, a private real estate investment trust that was formed in December of 1995 to acquire the Homart regional mall portfolio from Sears, Roebuck and Co S.N..
General Growth owns 38.2 percent of GGP/Homart Inc and accordingly, it indirectly owned that percentage of the mall.

The total amount paid for 100 percent of the mall was about $19.9 million. It included the assumption of $16.75 million of mortgage debt that matures in about 18 months and $3.15 million of cash and assumption of short-term liabilities. Annualized net operating income currently in place totals about $1.8 million.
Eden Prairie Center opened in 1976 and was substantially remodeled in 1989. It has about 984,000 total square feet of mall shop space.
General Growth owns interests in and/or manages 113 shopping malls in 38 states.
